title: Building a 6-DOF Robotic Arm with Computer Vision Sorting
summary: An intelligent robotic arm powered by Arduino and an OpenCV-driven Python camera feed that detects, sorts, and stacks colored components in real-time.

details.story: Industrial automation increasingly depends on smart sorting mechanisms where robotic manipulators perceive their environment before executing tasks. In this project designed for our high school AI & Robotics curriculum, students construct a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator armed with an overhead webcam. The Python script processes live frames using color thresholding and contour detection, sending Cartesian coordinates via serial communication to the Arduino microcontroller to calculate inverse kinematics on the fly.
steps: Assemble the aluminium 6-DOF chassis ensuring servo horns are properly calibrated at 90° neutral position.
Wire the PCA9685 PWM shield to the Arduino Mega via I2C (SDA -> Pin 20, SCL -> Pin 21) with common ground.
Mount the USB camera directly above the workspace at a fixed 45cm focal distance.
Calibrate camera distortion matrix and configure HSV color thresholds in OpenCV.
Execute the Python controller script to stream target coordinates to the Arduino.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Industrial automation increasingly depends on smart sorting mechanisms where robotic manipulators perceive their environment before executing physical tasks. In this project designed for our high school AI & Robotics curriculum, students construct a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator armed with an overhead webcam. The Python vision script processes live frames using color thresholding and contour detection, sending Cartesian coordinates via serial communication to the Arduino microcontroller to calculate inverse kinematics on the fly.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: The overhead camera continuously grabs 1080p frames at 30 FPS. The Python script isolates target objects using HSV thresholding, computes centroid centroids (Cx, Cy), and maps pixel coordinates to physical millimeter coordinates on the work surface. These target (X, Y, Z) vectors are sent over USB serial to the Arduino Mega, which runs trigonometric inverse kinematics algorithms to calculate exact pulse-width modulation values for each of the 6 MG996R metal-gear servos.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: Because 6 high-torque metal servos draw up to 6A stall current under load, a dedicated PCA9685 16-channel 12-bit PWM driver is powered directly by an external 5V 10A DC regulated power supply. The Arduino Mega communicates with the PCA9685 driver over the I2C bus (Pin 20 SDA, Pin 21 SCL) with a shared common ground, ensuring glitch-free actuation without microcontroller resets.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: We first flashed our servo calibration sketch to center all servos at exactly 90 degrees before fastening mechanical horn brackets. The Python OpenCV controller tests color identification by sorting blue, red, and yellow pucks into designated drop-off bins with sub-centimeter positional accuracy.

title: Autonomous Obstacle Avoidance AI Rover with LiDAR & SLAM
summary: Build an intelligent terrain rover that creates 2D floor plans using a 360° LiDAR sensor and navigates unknown rooms autonomously.

details.story: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the cornerstone of autonomous self-driving cars, warehouse AGVs, and interplanetary rovers. This project teaches students how to break down complex sensor fusion into tangible building blocks. By integrating an ESP32 microcontroller with a 360° 2D laser scanner, students visualize real-time point clouds on a local web dashboard and program reactive collision-avoidance algorithms.

hardware.item: 12V TT Geared DC Motors with Optical Encoders

steps: Fabricate the 4WD acrylic/aluminium chassis with suspension dampeners for smooth sensor rotation.
Connect RPLiDAR TX/RX to ESP32 Hardware Serial2 pins at 115200 baud.
Implement wheel encoder pulse interrupts to calculate dead-reckoning trajectory.
Stream polar coordinate vectors via WebSocket to the host computer.
Run Hector SLAM / Cartographer node to render live 2D obstacle heatmaps.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the cornerstone of autonomous self-driving vehicles, warehouse robots, and planetary rovers. This project demystifies complex sensor fusion into hands-on building blocks for students. By combining an ESP32 microcontroller with a 360-degree laser range scanner, students construct a rover that explores unknown indoor spaces and compiles 2D floor plans in real-time.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: The RPLiDAR A1 spins at 5.5 Hz, sending 8,000 laser distance points per second over UART serial to the ESP32. The microcontroller streams the polar coordinate packet over high-speed WebSocket Wi-Fi to a host workstation running ROS 2 Cartographer SLAM. The node calculates loop closures and builds occupancy grids while reactive PID controllers steer TT geared DC motors away from obstacles.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: A 3S 11.1V 2200mAh LiPo battery pack delivers raw voltage to an LM2596 buck converter tuned to 5.0V for the ESP32 and LiDAR, while motor power is routed through an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver. Hall-effect wheel encoders are wired to interrupt pins (GPIO 18, 19, 21, 22) for high-precision odometry feedback.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: Foxglove Studio visualizes real-time 2D laser point clouds. Students can watch live laser scans paint hallway walls, doorways, and obstacles, tuning the collision threshold so the rover smoothly routes around chair legs and moving objects without operator intervention.

title: Smart IoT Environmental & Greenhouse Station with OLED Telemetry
summary: A solar-assisted environmental telemetry node that tracks soil moisture, ambient humidity, temperature, and sun exposure with live cloud logging.

details.story: Global agriculture faces intense climate challenges. In this Atal Tinkering Lab staple project, young innovators construct an automated plant health monitoring device. Utilizing capacitive corrosion-resistant soil sensors, a precision DHT22 sensor, and an I2C OLED display, the station triggers automatic peristaltic drip irrigation whenever soil moisture falls below threshold levels.
steps: Calibrate capacitive sensor in dry air (raw 3400) and full water submersion (raw 1300).
Wire OLED display to ESP32 Pin 21 (SDA) and Pin 22 (SCL).
Configure Wi-Fi credentials and publish sensor readings to MQTT topic every 30 seconds.
Add hysteresis logic to relay control to prevent erratic pump cycling.
Hook up solar panel with diode protection to charge the 18650 lithium battery.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Modern agriculture faces extreme climate variability and water shortages. In this Atal Tinkering Lab staple project, young innovators construct an automated plant health monitoring device. Utilizing corrosion-resistant capacitive soil sensors, precision DHT22 climate sensors, and an I2C OLED display, the station triggers automatic peristaltic drip irrigation whenever soil moisture drops below threshold levels.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: The station samples soil capacitance, ambient temperature, relative humidity, and solar light intensity every 15 seconds. Data is rendered on the local 0.96 inch SSD1306 OLED screen and simultaneously published over MQTT to a cloud dashboard. If moisture drops below 35%, a 5V relay energizes the submersible water pump for 4 seconds, followed by a soak delay to evaluate water absorption.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: Power is provided by a 6V 2W monocrystalline solar cell charging an 18650 lithium-ion cell via a TP4056 module with over-discharge protection. An ultra-low dropout 3.3V regulator powers the ESP32 in deep-sleep mode, enabling weeks of off-grid operation.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: Calibration was performed by taking baseline analog readings in dry air (raw 3400) and completely saturated soil (raw 1300). Hysteresis thresholds were programmed in firmware to prevent pump chatter during slight soil settling.

title: Interactive VR Physics & Mechanical Engineering Lab with Meta Quest
summary: How we deploy immersive 3D virtual reality simulations that let students disassemble complex jet engines and planetary gear sets in zero-risk environments.

details.story: Traditional textbook diagrams fail to convey how torque transfers through planetary gearboxes or how magnetic flux induces eddy currents. Through standalone Meta Quest VR headsets deployed in our AR/VR labs, students step inside complex machinery, pause time, alter gravity parameters, and manipulate microscopic atoms with their bare hands.
steps: Set up Guardian boundaries and enable Kiosk mode for seamless student onboarding.
Import SolidWorks CAD models into Unity with optimized decimation algorithms.
Apply PhysX continuous collision detection and realistic inertia tensor calculations.
Incorporate spatial audio cues for gear mesh friction and pneumatic pressure drops.
Implement educator dashboard for real-time progress assessment and synchronized multi-headset triggers.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Traditional 2D textbook diagrams fail to convey how torque transfers through planetary gearboxes or how magnetic flux induces eddy currents. Through standalone Meta Quest VR headsets deployed in our AR/VR labs, students step inside complex machinery, pause time, alter gravity parameters, and manipulate microscopic atoms with their bare hands in zero-risk environments.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: The simulation uses Unity 2024 LTS with the OpenXR plugin and PhysX physics engine. Students interact with gear teeth, pistons, and magnetic coils using ergonomic hand tracking or 6-DoF controllers with precision haptic feedback pulses simulating mechanical friction and gear teeth mesh.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: A dedicated Wi-Fi 6 access point creates a low-latency local network inside the lab, allowing the educator's tablet to mirror headsets, trigger simulated mechanical failures (e.g. sheared bolts or bearing seizures), and view real-time student quiz metrics.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: CAD assemblies from SolidWorks were decimated using Blender to retain visual fidelity while running smoothly at 90 FPS on mobile XR chipsets. Spatial audio triggers enhance spatial presence when mechanisms engage.

title: Custom Carbon-Fiber Quadcopter Drone with Optical Flow Stabilization
summary: Design and assemble an indoor-safe quadcopter flight platform with brushless ESCs, Betaflight firmware, and downward optical flow hovering.

details.story: Drone technology is transforming surveying, disaster management, and precision agriculture. In our senior STEM tinkering labs, students delve into PID tuning, aerodynamic thrust ratios, and flight dynamics. This hands-on build walks students through soldering high-frequency power distribution boards, configuring brushless motor timing, and setting up optical flow sensors for GPS-denied indoor hovering.

hardware.item: PMW3901 Optical Flow & VL53L1X LiDAR Combo

steps: Solder XT60 power lead and low-ESR 35V 1000uF capacitor to absorb motor voltage spikes.
Mount brushless motors, ensuring diagonal pairs spin clockwise and counter-clockwise respectively.
Connect optical flow sensor to UART6 with telemetry enabled in Betaflight ports.
Calibrate accelerometer and configure failsafe disarm triggers.
Tune Roll, Pitch, and Yaw PID loops for razor-sharp indoor hover stability.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Drone technology is transforming surveying, disaster management, and precision agriculture. In our senior STEM tinkering labs, students delve into PID tuning, aerodynamic thrust ratios, and flight dynamics. This hands-on build walks students through soldering high-frequency power distribution boards, configuring brushless motor timing, and setting up optical flow sensors for GPS-denied indoor hovering.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: The SpeedyBee F405 flight controller samples its BMI270 gyro at 3.2 kHz, running high-speed PID loops that send DShot600 digital pulse packets to 55A ESCs. A downward PMW3901 optical flow camera tracks ground textures while a VL53L1X time-of-flight laser altimeter holds altitude, allowing rock-solid indoor hovering without GPS satellites.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: High-temperature silicone wires (14 AWG) connect the XT60 connector to the 4-in-1 ESC board. A low-ESR 35V 1000uF electrolytic capacitor absorbs inductive voltage spikes caused by active motor braking. Motors are soldered directly to copper pads with clean solder fillets.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: Betaflight 10.10 Configurator was used to map motor rotation directions (Props In configuration), verify ELRS radio channel end-points (1000-2000us), and configure two-stage failsafe disarm triggers for student flight safety.

title: 3D-Printed Bionic Prosthetic Hand with Flex Sensor Teleoperation
summary: A wearable sensory glove that mirrors human finger motion to articulate a 3D-printed tendon-driven bionic hand using micro servos.

details.story: Empowering students to solve real-world accessibility challenges brings purpose to STEM education. In this project, high school students use CAD modelling in Onshape to print ergonomic phalanges in tough PETG filament, thread flexible braided fishing line as anatomical tendons, and attach 2.2-inch conductive flex sensors to a fabric glove. Every flex of the user's hand is instantly mirrored by the bionic replica.

hardware.item: SG90 / MG90S Metal Gear Micro Servos

steps: Slice and 3D print finger phalanges with 0.15mm layer height and 40% infill for joint durability.
Assemble fingers using elastic shock cords for passive extension and Kevlar lines for active flexion.
Sew flex sensors onto the control glove along knuckles with heat-shrink reinforcement.
Map analog voltage dividers (10k ohm reference resistor) from flex sensors to servo angles (0°-180°).
Calibrate resting hand offset values in EEPROM memory.

storySections.title: The Idea
storySections.text: Empowering students to solve real-world accessibility challenges brings profound purpose to STEM education. In this project, high school students use CAD modelling in Onshape to print ergonomic finger phalanges in tough PETG filament, thread flexible braided Spectra lines as anatomical tendons, and attach 2.2-inch conductive flex sensors to a wearable control glove. Every flex of the user's hand is instantly mirrored by the bionic replica.

storySections.title: How It Works
storySections.text: When a finger bends, the conductive carbon flex sensor changes its electrical resistance from 25k ohms (flat) to over 65k ohms (90 degree bend). The Arduino transmitter reads the resulting voltage divider signals, normalizes them between 0 and 180 degrees, and transmits 5-byte data packets via 2.4GHz NRF24L01+ transceivers to the bionic hand receiver.

storySections.title: Assembling the Electronics
storySections.text: Five metal-gear MG90S micro servos are anchored in the forearm chassis. Elastic silicone shock cords provide passive finger extension, while braided Spectra lines tied to servo horn pulleys provide active finger flexion, mimicking human flexor digitorum muscles.

storySections.title: Programming and Testing
storySections.text: We implemented moving-average filtering in Arduino firmware to filter out muscle tremors. Calibration offsets for flat and bent positions are stored in EEPROM, allowing user calibration without reflashing firmware.
